phases.title: Phase 1: Audit and reclassify (3 modules)
phases.strategy: Audit the module before extraction. If it matches the shared library pattern, treat it as high risk and handle it near the end of the plan.
phases.rollback: Document the fall-back procedure before starting this phase
phases.rationale: These modules could not be classified automatically. Audit them before starting extraction to determine the correct strangler strategy. Scope: 3 module(s), 8,286 LOC, 357 known vulnerabilities.

phases.title: Phase 2: Untangle shared legacy libraries (1 module)
phases.strategy: Identify consumers and lift the shared module into a versioned package. Extract one consumer at a time; deprecate the shared copy once all consumers migrate.
phases.rollback: Restore shared library import; republish legacy version
phases.rationale: Shared libraries are the hardest to extract — every consumer is affected. We handle them after leaf modules are stable so we can migrate consumers one at a time. Scope: 1 module(s), 261 LOC, 0 known vulnerabilities.

narrative: **Pre-assigned decision: REFACTOR** (phase Phase-2). Rationale: Nexus app — shared core data classes with modules outside the current tenant scope (cross-team coupling). Full refactor is multi-phase: extract outer API, lift shared models, introduce anti-corruption layer on the database, untangle the shared libraries, and WRAP the mainframe COBOL component behind a REST adapter. Never rewrite the COBOL core. The app-05 application contains 5 modules (8,582 lines of code, 357 known vulnerabilities). NexusForge proposes a 2-phase strangler decomposition covering shared, unknown. Total estimated effort: 52 engineer-days (~10 working weeks for a single engineer, or ~2 weeks for a 4-engineer team working in parallel). Each phase is independently deployable and reversible — no big-bang cut-over.
